reference_prolog:
/*  Self-contained SWI-Prolog program
    State: Montana
    Focus year: 2021
    Question: Must a landlord accept a tenant's attempt to cure for waste?

    Statute encoded: MT Code  70-24-422 (2021)
*/

% --------------------------
% Scenario facts (question statement)
% --------------------------

% Basic context
scenario_state(montana).
scenario_focus_year(2021).

% The tenant committed "waste": destroys/defaces/damages/impairs/removes part of the premises.
% This corresponds to MT Code  70-24-422(3), referring to violation of 70-24-321(2).
scenario_noncompliance_type(waste).

% Landlord delivered a written notice of termination for the waste noncompliance.
scenario_notice_delivered(yes).

% Time model (days after tenant receives the notice).
% receipt_day = 0, termination_day is the "date specified in the notice".
scenario_notice_receipt_day(0).
scenario_notice_termination_day(3).

% Tenant attempted to cure (repair/pay damages) before the termination date.
scenario_tenant_attempted_cure(yes).
scenario_tenant_cure_day(2).

% Landlord did NOT elect to use a separate 30-day notice procedure (70-24-441),
% so 70-24-422 governs.
scenario_landlord_elects_30_day_notice(no).

% Helper predicate that succeeds when the scenario statement is satisfied.
scenario_statement :-
    scenario_state(montana),
    scenario_focus_year(2021),
    scenario_noncompliance_type(waste),
    scenario_notice_delivered(yes),
    scenario_notice_receipt_day(0),
    scenario_notice_termination_day(3),
    scenario_tenant_attempted_cure(yes),
    scenario_tenant_cure_day(2),
    scenario_landlord_elects_30_day_notice(no).

% --------------------------
% Utility predicates
% --------------------------

% before_or_on_day(D1, D2) is true when D1 =< D2.
before_or_on_day(D1, D2) :-
    integer(D1),
    integer(D2),
    D1 =< D2.

% --------------------------
% Statute translations (MT Code  70-24-422 (2021))
% --------------------------

/*
  MT Code  70-24-422(7) (2021):
  "The landlord is not bound by this section in the event that the landlord elects
   to use the 30-day notice for termination of tenancy as provided in 70-24-441."
*/
statute_70424422_applies :-
    scenario_landlord_elects_30_day_notice(no).

/*
  MT Code  70-24-422(1)(a) (2021):
  General cure provision for certain noncompliance:
  If noncompliance is remediable by repairs, payment of damages, or written approval
  and tenant remedies before the notice termination date, then rental agreement does not terminate.

  We model this as a "cure blocks termination" rule for noncompliance handled under subsection (1),
  but NOT for special termination paths in subsections (2)-(4) unless those subsections provide a cure.
*/
statute_70424422_1a_cure_blocks_termination(NoncomplianceType) :-
    statute_70424422_applies,
    statute_noncompliance_handled_under_subsection_1(NoncomplianceType),
    statute_noncompliance_remediable(NoncomplianceType),
    scenario_tenant_attempted_cure(yes),
    scenario_tenant_cure_day(CureDay),
    scenario_notice_termination_day(TermDay),
    before_or_on_day(CureDay, TermDay).

/*
  MT Code  70-24-422(3) (2021):
  If tenant destroys/defaces/damages/impairs/removes part of premises (waste),
  landlord may terminate upon giving 3 days' written notice and tenant shall vacate
  if landlord terminates. No cure right is stated in subsection (3).
*/
statute_70424422_3_special_termination_path_applies :-
    statute_70424422_applies,
    scenario_noncompliance_type(waste),
    scenario_notice_delivered(yes),
    scenario_notice_receipt_day(ReceiptDay),
    scenario_notice_termination_day(TermDay),
    integer(ReceiptDay),
    integer(TermDay),
    TermDay - ReceiptDay >= 3.

% Classification: which noncompliance types are handled under subsection (1)?
% Waste is handled under subsection (3), so it is NOT in subsection (1)'s cure framework.
statute_noncompliance_handled_under_subsection_1(unauthorized_pet).
statute_noncompliance_handled_under_subsection_1(unauthorized_persons).
statute_noncompliance_handled_under_subsection_1(verbal_abuse).
statute_noncompliance_handled_under_subsection_1(other_remediable_noncompliance).

% Remediability (for subsection (1)(a) logic). Waste might be physically remediable,
% but because waste is governed by subsection (3), we do not route it through (1)(a).
statute_noncompliance_remediable(unauthorized_pet).
statute_noncompliance_remediable(unauthorized_persons).
statute_noncompliance_remediable(verbal_abuse).
statute_noncompliance_remediable(other_remediable_noncompliance).

/*
  Derived statutory consequence:
  Landlord is REQUIRED to accept the cure (i.e., cannot terminate on that notice)
  only when a statute says cure blocks termination.
*/
statute_landlord_must_accept_cure_for_noncompliance(NoncomplianceType) :-
    statute_70424422_1a_cure_blocks_termination(NoncomplianceType).

% --------------------------
% Legal reasoning for this question
% --------------------------

% In this scenario, determine if the landlord must accept the tenant's attempt to cure.
landlord_must_accept_tenant_cure :-
    scenario_statement,
    scenario_noncompliance_type(NoncomplianceType),
    statute_landlord_must_accept_cure_for_noncompliance(NoncomplianceType).

% If the waste special termination path applies, cure is not a statutory bar under 70-24-422(3).
% Therefore there is no statutory "must accept" obligation under this section for waste.
landlord_not_required_to_accept_cure_for_waste :-
    scenario_statement,
    statute_70424422_3_special_termination_path_applies.

% --------------------------
% Answer
% --------------------------

housing_answer(yes) :-
    landlord_must_accept_tenant_cure,
    !.
housing_answer(no) :-
    landlord_not_required_to_accept_cure_for_waste,
    !.
housing_answer(no) :-
    % Default: if no statute-based duty to accept cure is proven, answer is "no".
    scenario_statement,
    !.

% --------------------------
% Main entrypoint (required)
% --------------------------

main :-
    housing_answer(Result),
    format('housing_answer(~w).~n', [Result]).


:- initialization(main, main).

expected.question: Must a landlord accept a tenant's attempt to cure for waste?
